It is the name of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Hagar's first child, born as a fulfillment of a divine promise. In these traditions, Ismaaeel is considered the father of the Arab peoples, making the name a reference to Arab identity and heritage.

Additionally, the story of Ibrahim and Ismaaeel teaches valuable lessons about faith, perseverance, and the importance of trusting in Allah's divine plan. Through this name, Muslims are reminded of their connection to a long lineage of devout believers and are encouraged to follow in their footsteps in seeking nearness to Allah.
